name: Run: DOMAIN-MODEL-FOUNDATION (5 tickets)
description: OUTCOME full-success (no mid-run stop-and-ask; only per-ticket checkpoints). PAUSE-CAUSE none. FRICTION: all gate refactors self-resolved. T3 IT gate caught an OffsetDateTime auditing DateTimeProvider bug (prod fix). T5 headline e2e bug: newman env-scope shadowed collection-scope ids -> /catalogs// 404; fixed by keeping chained ids in collection scope (mx-ecc3ef). PLANNING-GAP->FIX: (a) pin the OffsetDateTime/@EnableJpaAuditing DateTimeProvider requirement as an acceptance note (recurs in later slices, mx-5fb01d); (b) state the newman env-vs-collection variable-scope rule as an e2e precondition in 10-QA; (c) add a slice-zero repo-hygiene precheck (ignore bin/, *.factorypath). QA: no post-run deep-review; issues caught in-run.

name: Run: LIBRARY-SPINE (7 tickets)
description: OUTCOME full-success. PAUSE-CAUSE none. FRICTION: two SUBSTANTIVE gate fixes, both agent-resolved. T3: manager read @OpaPreAuthorize off the proxied INTERFACE method -> annotation missed -> silent abstain = every call allowed (a fail-open); fixed via AopUtils.getMostSpecificMethod (mx-b9619b). T5: two build/runtime breakers in one ticket - starter exposed a primary ObjectMapper so Boot's Jackson backed off (every OffsetDateTime 500'd, mx-6023c0), and AbacFilter didn't override the anonymous token (every /api/** 403'd, mx-410831). PLANNING-GAP->FIX: (a) make proxied-method-annotation resolution an explicit acceptance/test for any custom AuthorizationManager<MethodInvocation> (silent-abstain is an invisible fail-open); (b) pin the starter Jackson/ObjectMapper bean policy (never register a primary mapper; use ObjectProvider) in 00-DESIGN; (c) state the AbacFilter-must-beat-AnonymousAuthenticationToken ordering invariant as acceptance. All three became Mulch records that SHOULD have been planning inputs. QA: no post-run deep-review.

name: Run: USER-MANAGEMENT-SERVICE (9 tickets)
description: OUTCOME full-success. PAUSE-CAUSE none (Decisions sections are documented design choices, not mid-run questions). FRICTION: T4 test-harness refactor - dogfood test drove acting identity via a ThreadLocal that never crossed the Tomcat HTTP boundary -> allow-paths failed, deny-paths passed for the wrong reason; fixed to a request header + one security chain (a 2nd /** chain tripped Spring Security 6.4 'already configured') + @ConditionalOnBean on the null-filter FilterRegistrationBean. T5 duplicate requireSubsetOfActor across two services extracted to a shared SubsetGuard. T9 needed deterministic e2e data keyed on runtime subs/catalog id -> idempotent internal bootstrap surface. PLANNING-GAP->FIX: (a) pre-specify the dogfood-test rig (identity travels IN the HTTP request, one security chain, @ConditionalOnBean filter registration) - the ThreadLocal-across-HTTP trap is a pure rig gotcha; (b) name the single SubsetGuard seam up front (docs said shared but it got duplicated then refactored); (c) make runtime-sub-keyed e2e seeding a planned T-item, not an in-gate improvisation. QA: no post-run deep-review.

name: Run: TAG-DICTIONARY (6 tickets)
description: OUTCOME full-success - smoothest run of the six; tag matrix 7/7 through the gateway. PAUSE-CAUSE none. FRICTION: no substantive gate refactors (reviews found nothing invented), only small tidies. Notable SELF-MADE correctness decision (T3, recorded as decision not pause): fail-closed has TWO shapes - a role-supplier fails closed to EMPTY, but a validation-input dictionary fetch must fail closed to a REJECTION (503), because an empty set would WIDEN legality. PLANNING-GAP->FIX: 00-DESIGN should distinguish the two fail-closed shapes explicitly (empty-deny for decision suppliers vs reject-503 for validation-input fetches) - the agent had to reason it out mid-ticket and it is an externally-visible contract choice. The team:define-tags=owner+admin capability split landed cleanly BECAUSE the prior slice's capability ladder existed (pinning the ladder pays forward). QA: no post-run deep-review.

name: Run: DATA-FILTERING (7 tickets) - the ONE paused run
description: OUTCOME paused-and-asked (the only genuine mid-run pause across all six slices). PAUSE-CAUSE (T6, class: UNDECIDED EXTERNALLY-VISIBLE BEHAVIOR / fail-open contract choice): the maintainer chose full scalar+array consistency for the list filter (over scalar-only) so list and single-GET decide the SAME rows; the filter residual maps to CONTAINS (the ? existence op, scalar+array). This is the contract for WHICH ROWS A LIST RETURNS - a matching-semantics fork the docs didn't pin. (Separately T1 self-caught an INVERTED ALLOW_ALL/DENY_ALL table in 00-DESIGN - a would-be whole-table fail-open leak - corrected against an empirical OPA probe rather than asking.) PLANNING-GAP->FIX: 00-DESIGN must PIN scalar-vs-array tag matching up front (externally-visible fail-open: does a scalar tag satisfy a membership grant; do list and single-GET agree?) AND verify the OPA partial-eval ALLOW_ALL/DENY_ALL mapping against a real probe before the run (an inverted mapping is a silent whole-table leak). Both are 'design resolves the fail-open semantics, not the implementer.' QA: merged via PR #11 (squash 473fde8); opa test 60/60, gateway 16/16; no separate deep-review.

name: Run: HIERARCHY-SINGLE-RESOURCE (7 tickets, Slice 5.5-A)
description: OUTCOME full-success mid-run (T1-T7 ran ticket-to-ticket, no stop-and-ask); the maintainer-facing issues came AFTER, in a separate deep-review. FRICTION: T3 IT caught re-parent SQL using subpath(path,oldDepth) uniformly -> Postgres 'invalid positions'; fixed with a CASE (mx-576e71). T6 example IT surfaced that a single-table subtree UPDATE doesn't reach descendants in ANOTHER table (a re-parented Category left Products on the old lineage) -> added library reparentDescendantsInTable. T7 'Docker unreachable' was a false negative (timeout not on PATH silently errored the probe). PLANNING-GAP->FIX: the decomposition ASSUMED a single-table hierarchy; the catalog's Category->Product spans two tables, forcing a cross-table re-parent invented at T6. 00-DESIGN should pin 'the re-parent rewrite must cover EVERY table the subtree spans' as explicit acceptance (load-bearing for the re-parent-flips-a-decision guarantee). POST-RUN deep-review (PR #14): 2 Medium, 0 Critical, both fixed. M1 reparentCategory used unlocked findById (deviated from lock-first mutate); M2 the e2e inheritance-200 didn't ISOLATE THE CUT (reader seeded catalog:[read] AND category:[read], so the direct grant alone passed even with inherited_grant deleted) - the clearest agentic-laziness instance (asserted shape, not cut). LESSON: e2e must assert the cut, and the deep-review autonomous-run lens catches what the run's own gate missed.

name: Autonomous-run synthesis: the two recurring planning-gap classes
description: Across the first 6 slices, ONLY ONE true mid-run pause occurred (DATA-FILTERING T6, on scalar-vs-array matching semantics). Everything else the agent resolved itself at the architecture-review gate. The high-value lesson for planning the NEXT slice is that the things that DID cause a pause or a substantive gate-refactor cluster into two classes: (1) 'DESIGN LEFT A FAIL-OPEN / CONTRACT SEMANTIC UNPINNED' - scalar-vs-array (DF-T6, paused), inverted ALLOW_ALL/DENY_ALL table (DF-T1), proxied-annotation silent-abstain (Spine-T3), two-shapes-of-fail-closed (Tag-T3), cross-table re-parent coverage (Hier-T6). These are the HIGHEST-value things to pre-resolve in 00-DESIGN/ADRs during phase-1 grill-me, because getting them wrong is a silent widening. (2) 'RIG / TEST-HARNESS GOTCHA DISCOVERED MID-RUN' - newman env-vs-collection scope (Domain-T5), OffsetDateTime auditing provider (Domain-T3), ThreadLocal-across-HTTP in dogfood tests (UMS-T4), runtime-sub-keyed e2e seeding (UMS-T9), timeout/Docker-probe PATH (Hier-T7). Most are now Mulch records that should be fed in as planning INPUTS, not rediscovered. ACTIONABLE: when decomposing a new slice, prime autonomous-runs and explicitly ask 'which fail-open/contract semantics are unpinned?' and 'which rig gotchas from prior runs apply here?' - that is what converts a paused run into a full-success run.

name: Run: HIERARCHY-LIST-FILTER (6 tickets, Slice 5.5-B)
description: OUTCOME: paused-and-asked ONCE, at T6 (the e2e), on a DESIGN FORK THE DOCS DID NOT COVER — the coarse type-level list gate. The type-level @OpaPreAuthorize(category:read) on listCategories evaluates allow with no ancestors, so a {catalog:[read]} inheritable subject (the one the widening exists for) was denied 403 before subtreeSpec could run; opa eval confirmed allow=false. Settled with the maintainer: add a small additive list-only allow clause (open the COARSE gate; fine cut stays in SQL). T1-T5 ran fully autonomous. A SECOND pause was a rig/environment blocker (NOT a design fork): the live e2e needs Docker Desktop but the rig had drifted between podman and docker engines; the maintainer restarted Docker, then the rig came up clean and the matrix ran 10/10 green. CHECKPOINT/TICKET FRICTION: every ticket's unit tests went green first-try after a real bug fix at the star gate, never a >3-attempt loop. The real bugs the star gates caught: T1 CTE id-IN bound String ids against a uuid column (operator does not exist: uuid = varchar) -> convert to UUID; T2 a test fixture put the inheritable grant under permissions[child] instead of permissions[ancestor/root] (the resolver was right, fixtures wrong) — the load-bearing list==single-GET-by-construction point; T4 the full-suite star run surfaced a THIRD @SpringBootConfiguration in the data.filter package (Found multiple) -> pin all three filter ITs with @ContextConfiguration, AND a subtreeOf-IT came back empty because the LtreePathSource must synthesize a catalog root path that lives in another table. T3 build-breaker (AbacQueryService ctor +AncestorResolver) caused NO test break because the 3-arg ctor was preserved; only the starter bean updated. PLANNING-GAP->FIX (keystone): (1) a list-WIDENING slice must ALSO open the coarse type-level list gate for inheritable grants — the design/ADR 0010 worked-trace assumed the inheritable subject reaches the list but never addressed the coarse gate; future hierarchy-list planning must pin the gate. (2) the slice-planner should note that subtreeOf reads the ROOT's path, which may live in a different table than the listed rows (a test-seeding contract point). (3) the DOCKER-vs-PODMAN engine split is a recurring rig gotcha — the e2e runner + E2E-TESTING should state 'bring the WHOLE rig up under ONE engine'. QA: the post-run /deep-review found NO Critical and ONE Medium — a stale byte-compatible Javadoc on the 3-arg findAuthorized (the notDenied filter is actually a fail-CLOSED hardening that closes a list<->single-GET fail-open gap on main); fixed doc-only. opa test 77/77; gradlew build green incl. HierarchyListFilterIT on real Postgres; e2e 10/10 through the gateway.

name: Run: REST-API-REFINEMENT / Phase 5.9 error contract (5 tickets)
description: OUTCOME + PAUSE-CAUSE: Full autonomous success, no pause for a missing decision. All five tickets (T1 library vocabulary/carrier/advice-base -> T2 catalog adoption -> T3 user-svc adoption -> T4 e2e -> T5 docs) ran T1..T5 in order with a checkpoint after each. ADR 0011 had deliberately pinned all five contract forks (depth=minimal-superset, clean-replacement, library-owned vocabulary, semantic-granularity, typed-in-spec), so the one recurring pause class (a fail-open/contract semantic left unpinned) did NOT recur. The only mid-run interactive moment was a deliberate AskUserQuestion at the T3 review gate to confirm a library REFACTOR scope (lift status() onto the ApiErrorCode interface vs keep a per-app helper) -- a design improvement the gate surfaced, not a blocker; the user chose lift-to-interface. CHECKPOINT/TICKET FRICTION: (1) T3 review-gate refactor (status() onto the interface) touched T1's already-committed ApiErrorCode + rippled to LibraryErrorCode/UserMgmtErrorCode/CatalogErrorCode + the U6 test -- landed in the T3 commit, T1 tests stayed green. (2) Two RIG/ENVIRONMENT friction events, both NOT code: the Testcontainers ITs first failed 'Could not find a valid Docker environment' because the podman machine reported running but its API socket file was missing (stale state) -> podman machine stop/start recreated it; and the e2e tag/team matrices first failed on user-svc endpoints because ./deploy.sh build rebuilds ONLY the catalog image (build_usermgmt_image is gated behind usermgmt_image_exists ||) so the usermgmt pod served 6-day-old code -> forced docker build of opa-abac-usermgmt:local + recreate. Both recorded as Mulch failures. PLANNING-GAP -> FIX: the decomposition could have pre-stated (a) that ApiErrorCode should carry status() from the start (T1) so T3 needed no interface refactor -- minor, the refactor was clean; and (b) that the e2e ticket must force-rebuild the usermgmt image when ENABLE_USER_SERVICE=1, since deploy.sh build silently skips it -- the autonomous prompt mentioned './deploy.sh build to force new app code into the pods' but that command does NOT cover the user-service, a real planning-gap to fix in the prompt template for any two-service slice. The catalog 403-via-gateway proof (which the catalog MockMvc permissive chain could not drive) was correctly deferred to e2e in the plan and passed. QA: the post-run /deep-review (adversarial general-purpose sub-agent over the whole branch vs main) found NO security regression -- same statuses, deny-renders-never-authorizes, core untouched, clean replacement, typed vocabulary, Location keyed by addressable id -- and exactly ONE Low doc-completeness nit (catalog spec defined a Forbidden response component referenced by 0 paths); fixed in a follow-up by wiring 403 onto all 13 gated catalog ops. No laziness signal: every ticket's tests assert the actual cut (the right errorCode per status, no message, nothing-stored on 503, real 403 deny end-to-end), not just response shape.

name: Run: PAGINATION-ENVELOPE (6 tickets)
description: OUTCOME full-success: T1–T6 executed in one session with zero pauses — no fork needed the maintainer (the 8 grill-me decisions pinned in ADR 0012 covered every semantic the run hit); first run under the new delegation policy (scout/validate sub-agents only — the T5 suite sweep + the 8-runner validation pass; all code in the main loop). PAUSE-CAUSE none. FRICTION (2 small, both fix-until-green within their ticket): [T3] the planned advice mapping was wrong in KIND — generated @Validated API interfaces raise ConstraintViolationException (AOP method validation), not HandlerMethodValidationException; one IT loop found it, and pinning the finding in STATUS-03 let T4 apply it directly with no loop. [T5] the new runner's direct-SQL catalog seed omitted the 5.5-A ltree path column -> category creation fail-closed ('parent has no path'); old matrices never trip it (their rows were backfilled by the adoption migration) — fixed in the runner only, T1–T4 stayed frozen. Review-gate value: T1's gate caught the load-bearing composition duplicated between unpaged/paged paths (extracted to one authorizedSpec helper); T3's caught an orphaned repo method. PLANNING-GAP->FIX: (1) decomposition could pre-pin the param-validation exception type for spec-generated @RequestParam constraints (one sentence in the ticket would have saved the only red-test loop); (2) the QA conventions said 'in-process HttpServer OPA stub' but the module's real ITs use a programmable stub OpaClient — harmless, but conventions sections should be grounded in the named exemplar files; (3) e2e runner checklists should include 'seed catalogs WITH ltree path' since 5.5-A (now a failure record). QA: unit 126 + catalog 35 + user-svc 77 + e2e 128 assertions green; /deep-review pending (phase 4).

name: Run: RESOURCE-RESOLUTION (7 tickets)
description: OUTCOME: full success — fully autonomous T1-T7, zero pauses, no design fork reopened; both decomposition-pinned semantics (missing-id 403; tags_satisfied conjunct) held through implementation, e2e, and review. CHECKPOINT/TICKET FRICTION: T6 had the only fix-until-green loop, both rig-class: (1) the fixture-catalog psql seed lacked the ltree path (modeled on run-tag-matrix.sh whose pathless INSERT only works on persisted volumes) — first matrix run failed 500 fail-closed, fixed with the run-pagination-matrix.sh path+conflict-repair shape; (2) I5's planned FK-violation route was impossible (every FK is ON DELETE CASCADE) — substituted a deterministic stale-@Version save via a before-save aspect hook. Minor: T3 flipped ResourceResolutionSupport accessors package-private->public for the starter test (named deviation); a T6 amend had to redo a collection edit text-level because json.dump reformatted a hand-formatted file. PLANNING-GAP->FIX: (a) the decomposition's e2e conventions should name the SEEDING MODEL explicitly (run-pagination-matrix.sh, delete-then-seed + ltree path) — the prompt pointed at run-tag-matrix.sh which carries a latent pathless seed; (b) I4/I5 acceptance offered 'a stale save OR an FK violation' — a 30s schema check at decompose time (all FKs CASCADE) would have pinned the only viable mechanism; (c) add a runner-hygiene checklist line to future e2e tickets (delete-then-seed, self-restart OPA when the slice edits policies) — all three deep-review findings were exactly this class. QA: post-run /deep-review (8-lens adversarial workflow, 13 agents) found 0 Critical, 0 library/security/concurrency findings, 3 e2e-harness hygiene findings (fixed + sibling-swept same commit) — no laziness/bias/drift signal in code or tests.

name: Run: PERMISSION-CATEGORIES (8 tickets)
description: OUTCOME full-success: T1-T8 implemented, tested, and committed in one autonomous session with zero maintainer pauses; the five pinned decomposition semantics + the ten pinned forks answered every fork that arose. PAUSE-CAUSE none. FRICTION: (1) T2 - the decomposition's filter sketch ('list' in effective_actions(...)) does not FOLD under partial evaluation (OPA never inlines user functions over unknown args); resolved in-run by empirical 'opa eval --partial' prototyping before writing - the pinned P10 acceptance caught it; (2) T4 - the spec's '(integer enum)' parenthetical for roleLevel conflicted with the QA-pinned uniform 422 (codegen enums answer 400 at deserialization); QA cells won; (3) T5 - two test-shape reworks at the review gate (the designed admin-denial cell cannot ride HTTP because custom level-30 codes carry no team:manage - the I12 pin itself; the first latch-cell tier pairing could not distinguish stale-read from lock-read); (4) T6 - the decomposition assumed all three types carry tags on the wire; only CategoryRequest does, so the delta dispatch is category-scoped and two contracts re-pinned with rationale (missing-id PUT 404; the I4 race window moved to the catalog PUT); (5) T7 - ONE flipped cell (E1b 204): the fixture over-granted catalog WRITE and inherited_grant covers subtree deletes through the ancestor type's effective set - the DESIGNED per-type denial semantic; fixture corrected, subtlety documented; also jsonb '?' operator eaten by JDBC in the Liquibase sweep (loop #1 of T3). PLANNING-GAP->FIX: (a) when a decomposition sketches a PE-path rego formulation, REQUIRE an opa-eval-partial prototype as a decomposition-time gate, not an implementation discovery; (b) when pinning a wire-contract field, state the SCHEMA posture (schema-required/enum vs service-enforced) explicitly - the 422-vs-400 split is a recurring trap; (c) decompositions that say 'all three types/handlers' should name the wire-surface evidence (which request models actually carry the field) - reachability decides where a mechanism can live; (d) e2e cells involving tier-with-denial actors need their construction path named at decomposition time (custom codes lack manage - the designed cell needs a system-row tweak). QA: /deep-review (phase 4) pending - the maintainer runs it next.

name: QA addendum: Run PERMISSION-CATEGORIES — deep-review findings vs the run's own gates
description: QA (phase-4 deep-review, 2026-06-12, fix commit 136e826): the multi-lens review confirmed 17 findings (4 Critical) against the run's zero-pause T1-T8. Two Criticals were pre-existing/tracked (the B2 realm-fallback-on-outage class, now AGGRAVATED by 6.5: denied_actions/required_tags narrowing evaporates on the failure path — B2's priority should rise). Two Criticals + two Mediums were the run's own misses, ALL ONE SHAPE — the ticket's ★ review swept exactly the surface the ticket named and stopped there: T5 reviewed the grant gates but not their revoke/demote mirror (senior-removes-admin escalation); T6 verified the dispatch decisions but not the version binding of every downstream mutation branch (the reparent branch); T6's action sweep covered annotation strings but not the Java emitters/consumers of the old vocabulary (demo supplier; the resolver verb — the widening died silently behind a fail-closed degrade that kept e2e green). PLANNING-GAP->FIX for the next slice's decomposition: (1) a vocabulary migration ticket carries a grep-derived list of every Java emitter/consumer, not just annotations; (2) a new grant-path gate gets its revoke/demote mirror as an explicit QA row; (3) a dispatch decided on a loaded entity names the version-binding path for EVERY downstream mutation branch; (4) a fail-closed degrade can mask a feature regression — green e2e is not proof a widening/optimization path engaged; pin engagement separately (parity test or a distinguishing assertion).

name: Run: B2-SUPPLIER-OUTAGE (5 tickets)
description:
OUTCOME: full autonomous success — T1-T5 implemented, validated, and merged (PR #37 squash a97b3f2) with NO pause-to-ask. Every fail-open/contract semantic was pre-pinned by the planning package (ADR 0014 + 00-DESIGN + the two decomposition-pinned semantics), which is exactly what converts a paused run into a full-success run (the recurring planning-gap class did not recur).

CHECKPOINT/TICKET FRICTION: none substantive. No ticket needed a refactor at the ★ gate (each STATUS recorded 'nothing substantive' truthfully — the changes are verbatim-shape mirrors of the existing AncestorResolutionException / broad-catch families). No fix-until-green loops beyond first-compile import additions (logger fields in HierarchicalAuthorizer + CategoryListAuthorizer). One pre-existing-behavior test update: 3 HttpRoleDefinitionSupplierTest cells asserted the OLD swallow-to-empty posture and were correctly flipped to assert throws (not a defect — the strict classification is the point).

PLANNING-GAP -> FIX: essentially none. The one friction the planning FLAGGED (injecting a throwing RoleDefinitionSupplier test bean for SupplierOutageGateIT) was a non-issue — ResourceResolutionGateIT's @TestConfiguration bean-override idiom fit directly (a 4-line ToggleableRoleSupplier). The one genuine rig/environment gotcha: the podman CLI intermittently returns EMPTY output when invoked from the agent's Bash shell (works fine via 'podman run --rm' inside newman, and when fully detached) — this made a scripted stop-usermgmt outage cell unreliable, so the OPTIONAL live outage cell was DEFERRED (recorded, not silent-capped; the cut is already deterministic in the IT). FIX FOR NEXT TIME: planning/decomposition should mark any 'live stop-a-container' e2e cell as optional up front and note the podman-CLI-in-agent-shell flakiness so the run doesn't spend effort on it; the deterministic IT is the load-bearing proof.

QA: phase-④ multi-lens adversarial /deep-review (8 lenses -> refute -> completeness critic) found 0 confirmed, 0 refuted — the run's own ★ gates missed nothing (no laziness/self-preferential-bias/goal-drift). opa test 157/157, full build green, 10/10 newman matrices (167 assertions). Branch single-repo, bare-prompt phase-③ (no resume needed) — consistent with mx-70582b.
